items.title: New Brunswick utility is proposing rate hikes over next three years
items.excerpt: New Brunswick's public utility is proposing to raise electricity rates by an average of 5.5 per cent for each of the next three years.

items.title: B.C. rolling out fall vaccine program as flu cases circulating
items.excerpt: In an update on Wednesday, B.C.'s provincial health officer, Dr. Bonnie Henry, said free vaccines will be available against influenza, COVID-19 and others.

items.title: Child safety advocate says N.S. changes to car seat rules makes province ‘leader’ in country
items.excerpt: Nova Scotia has released the first set of regulations under its new Traffic Safety Act, which includes Canada's first age-based minimums for children's car seats.

items.title: Don’t target all students for possible OSAP misuse at a few schools, association says
items.excerpt: Career Colleges Ontario is urging Queen's Park to reinstate financial aid for career college students who were already approved for funds and are actively attending classes.

items.title: Crown seeks 2-year jail term for B.C. driver in baby stroller hit-and-run
items.excerpt: Kyle Nicholas Luca, 31, pleaded guilty in September to impaired driving causing bodily harm and failing to stop at an accident involving bodily harm.

items.title: Police seek witnesses after Vaughan hit-and-run that killed woman
items.excerpt: Police are reminding the public anyone who assists a suspect by concealing, repairing or altering a vehicle to avoid detection may face charges.

items.title: Stamps, Lions can clinch playoff berths with wins
items.excerpt: The task before the B.C. Lions and Calgary Stampeders this week is a very simple one.

items.title: Joly threatens ‘full force of the law’ over Cleveland-Cliffs’ Stelco job commitments
items.excerpt: Canada's industry minister said Wednesday Stelco Holdings Inc. cannot use the trade war to justify cutting jobs it committed to when it bought the Hamilton, Ont.-based steel plant.

items.title: Canned, frozen vegetable merger cancelled after Competition Bureau push
items.excerpt: Canada's Competition Bureau says it is 'pleased' a proposed merger, that would have seen two frozen and canned vegetable companies in Canada become one, has been terminated.

items.title: ‘Deeply grateful’: Biscuit the bunny returns home after cash reward posted
items.excerpt: Biscuit, an award-winning rabbit that was stolen from the Markham Fair last weekend, has been returned to its family, festival organizers say.

items.title: Halle Berry accuses ex-husband Olivier Martinez of turning son against her
items.excerpt: Halle Berry's legal filing comes after Olivier Martinez filed for sole custody and a domestic violence restraining order against the actor on Oct. 1.

items.title: Oilers acquire forward Hallander from Penguins
items.excerpt: The Edmonton Oilers acquired centre Filip Hallander from the Pittsburgh Penguins on Wednesday in exchange for defenceman Spencer Stastney.

items.title: Parti Québécois will request recount in Montreal-area riding
items.excerpt: PQ candidate Stephan Fogaing trailed Quebec Liberal candidate Affine Lwalalika by 10 votes in the initial results in the Vachon riding, on Montreal's south shore.

items.title: Canada won’t expand MAID for mental illness alone, minister says
items.excerpt: Currently, the law excludes MAID for people seeking it on grounds of mental illness, but the exception is set to expire in March 2027.

items.title: Ottawa teacher ‘immediately removed’ after sex assault allegation: board
items.excerpt: An Ottawa Catholic School Board teacher has been arrested and is charged with sexual and violent offences that allegedly involved a student.

items.title: Woman dead after fire at Montreal homeless encampment
items.excerpt: Montreal Mayor Soraya Martinez Ferrada says the woman's death at the encampment serves as a reminder of the importance of eliminating homelessness.

items.title: Curaleaf sweetens Aurora Cannabis takeover offer after past rejection
items.excerpt: Curaleaf says it's boosting its bid despite Aurora rebuffing past overtures because it wants to signal good faith negotiations and show it's worth combining the businesses.

items.title: First Nation demands more info on Bell AI data centre near Regina: ‘We have to live here’
items.excerpt: The Standing Buffalo Dakota Nation penned a letter to Bell Canada requesting documentation and information regarding the AI data centre that is under construction near Regina.

items.title: Catholic, Anglican bishops urge Albertans to consider referendum’s impact on vulnerable
items.excerpt: The Anglican bishops said they don't normally wade into political issues, but the referendum questions ultimately come down to choosing what kind of society we aspire to have.

items.title: Kingston Police officer charged with impaired driving while off duty
items.excerpt: A 26-year member of the Kingston Police was arrested in late September and accused of impaired driving while off duty.

items.title: Rideshare driver charged for alleged sexual assault of passenger in Winnipeg
items.excerpt: A rideshare driver was arrested late last month and is facing charges for the alleged sexual assault of a passenger in Winnipeg, WPS said.

items.title: Toronto police officer faces impaired driving charge after found asleep behind wheel
items.excerpt: The 51-year-old inspector has been with the police for 30 years and was assigned to 55 Division. He has been suspended with pay.

items.title: 2nd potential AI data centre worries Saint John residents: ‘We have questions’
items.excerpt: A second potential A.I. data centre in Saint John, N.B., is raising new questions for residents already fighting one proposed near the community of Lorneville.

items.title: U.S. officials allow liquor deliveries to resume to isolated New Brunswick island
items.excerpt: New Brunswick’s provincial liquor agency says it has resumed deliveries to an isolated island where the only land route is through Maine.

items.title: Suncor sells of N.L. offshore assets, other oilsands giant bulks up Alberta holdings
items.excerpt: Suncor is selling offshore assets in Atlantic Canada as it focuses on its oilsands holdings, while Cenovus is buying a smaller peer to grow its own footprint in northern Alberta.

items.title: Cenovus Energy looks to grow as it signs $5.7B deal to buy Athabasca Oil
items.excerpt: Athabasca Oil has 40,000 barrels per day of oilsands production currently, but Cenovus Energy sees the opportunity to ratchet that up to 115,000 by 2032.
